title: 2008 HMMT February Guts Problem 2
statement: Given right triangle \(A B C\), with \(A B=4, B C=3\), and \(C A=5\). Circle \(\omega\) passes through \(A\) and is tangent to \(B C\) at \(C\). What is the radius of \(\omega\) ?

solutions.text: \(\quad \frac{25}{8}\) Let \(O\) be the center of \(\omega\), and let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(A C\). Since \(O A=O C\), \(O M \perp A C\). Also, \(\angle O C M=\angle B A C\), and so triangles \(A B C\) and \(C M O\) are similar. Then, \(C O / C M=\) \(A C / A B\), from which we obtain that the radius of \(\omega\) is \(C O=\frac{25}{8}\).
